bugs.summary: byte-compiled [<- error can access a collected call during error reporting

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
A byte-compiled subassignment can construct a new language object for its error call. If garbage collection reclaims that call while the error is being formatted, R can abort instead of reporting the ordinary assignment error. This was found by OSS-Fuzz's eval fuzzer with the 34-byte input `x <- list(); x; x[2] <- x$a*9999` (testcase 6567538138611712, R source r90766).

Reproducible example:

Start an R-devel build configured with --enable-strict-barrier, with R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL and R_ENABLE_JIT=0, then run:

    x <- 1
    code <- compiler::compile(quote(x[1] <- integer(0)))
    gctorture2(1, inhibit_release = TRUE)
    eval(code)

On a pre-fix strict-barrier ASan build, this entered the "no more error handlers available (recursive errors?)" fallback. OSS-Fuzz reported "unprotected object ... (was LANGSXP)" in deparse2buff() and aborted. The expected result is the ordinary error "replacement has length zero"; the patched R-devel build produces it.

Analysis:

VectorAssign() raises the replacement-length error. error() obtains a call through getCurrentCall(), which can invoke R_getBCInterpreterExpression() and inflate the byte-compiled assignment into a fresh LANGSXP. errorcall() passed that call through vsignalError() and verrorcall_dflt() without protecting it. A collection before deparse1s(call) can therefore reclaim it. The patch was generated against trunk r90783.

Proposed patch: attached as protect-error-call.diff. It protects the call in errorcall() for the duration of this non-returning error path. The patch applies with patch -p0 against clean trunk r90783.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/416, where CI results can be seen.
